source_refs.note: 3. Elliptical Polarization: a main subheading of 8.2 Types of polarization, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 176-176.

blocks.text: A combination of linear and circular polarization, where the electric field vector traces an elliptical path is called elliptical polarization. In elliptical polarization as shown in Fig.8.4(c), the two components of electric field Eₓ and E_y are not equal and/or they differ in phase by an arbitrary angle θ. Example is the light passing through a stress plate or a waveplate.

blocks.alt: A tilted ellipse centred where the x and y axes cross. Black arrows E_x along x and E_y along y start at the centre. A cyan line along the long axis is marked a, a magenta line along the short axis is marked b, and a curved arrow theta turns from the y axis to the long axis.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4 (c): Elliptical polarization of light (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4 (c)).
